scope: Report-tab and main-menu navigation, local working tree only; not deployed.

environment.server: Reused existing server on port 3000; did not start or restart a server.
environment.data: Existing configured Supabase data read only. No business records or permissions changed.
environment.production: Production was not modified or measured for this phase. These are local development timings, not production guarantees.

methodology: Browser markers separate navigation-to-commit, immediate pending feedback, server authentication, data loading, calculations, and response-to-commit.

Final animation-frame sampling records whether the previous heading remains visible until the new instrumented page commits. This is a visibility/commit measurement, not a pure rendering CPU benchmark.

Cold means the scoped report data cache expired or was invalidated; repeated visits occurred within the existing 30-second freshness window. Development compilation/HMR samples are excluded from final comparison.

A synthetic browser fixture uses the actual navigation components, button-lock component, error UI, and persistent Suspense boundary with delayed/held/failed responses. It performs no business requests or writes.
findings_fixed: Report filters performed full document GET reloads despite warm data.
Global duplicate-submit action locks blocked a newer filter for 1500ms even after the previous report finished. Only report GET navigation now opts out; mutation locks remain.
Next route loading boundaries are keyed by child pathname and replaced current content. One explicit Suspense boundary in the persistent shell now retains the current workspace.
Hover/focus timers could start a redundant preload after a click. Clicking cancels the timer; active navigation suppresses preloading.
Ordinary query-envelope failures bypassed the route error boundary and lacked retry. Both error paths now offer a server refresh.

changes.navigation: Client router transitions, latest intent wins, native link semantics and GET fallback retained.
changes.pending: Destination label, selected-link ring, aria-busy and polite status; after 10 seconds, a retry destination link.
changes.filters: Client GET navigation, committed URL keys reset inputs correctly on history navigation; rapid newer filters remain allowed.
changes.content: Current workspace stays visible until destination resolves; query errors replace obsolete totals with an accessible error and retry.

preload.budget: One request in flight; at most two starts per 10 seconds; same canonical target suppressed for 20 seconds.
preload.exclusions: Nonempty customer/product/rep filters, other reports, current canonical destination, active navigation, hidden page, Save-Data and slow-2G/2G connections.
preload.authorization: Fresh reports permission, profitability permission, authenticated client and current center scope precede preload. Raw data keys retain actor, permissions, scope, filters and mutation generation. Actual router pushes still authenticate; no prefetched RSC page is retained.
preload.response: Empty response with private,no-store; failures do not block navigation.
preload.freshness: Uses the existing report data cache and invalidation mechanism. No additional stale window or authorization cache was added.

changes.instrumentation: Pending-feedback milliseconds and frame retention added to existing opt-in page diagnostics.

preload_experiment.procedure: Refresh data on Recent Orders invalidated the cache and refilled the Recent query. Focus Overview deliberately, complete independent fixture checks, then navigate to Overview.
preload_experiment.result: Overview commerce and production were warm on the actual visit; actual authorization still ran.

recent_orders_experiment.result: Latest selected report committed with complete ten-order data.

summary.note: One initial sampled frame preceded pending feedback. All sampled frames retained the previous useful content until commit.

browser_checks: Live report switch shows pending label while previous report remains visible.
Live main menu Reports → Dashboard → Orders → Reports retains content and pending feedback through the data load.
Four consecutive rapid live filters commit correctly after the button-lock fix.
Live report tabs and product filters restore correctly on back/forward.
Held B followed by C commits C; releasing old B never overwrites it.
Current route A → held B → A cancels the obsolete intent.
Held older filter followed by a newer product/customer filter commits the latest filter.
Back during pending navigation supersedes the outstanding request; forward restores the intended report/filter.
Injected fixture failure clears pending, hides obsolete totals, exposes alert and retry; retry recovers.
Held request beyond 10 seconds exposes explanatory slow state and destination reload link.
Keyboard focus preloads only allowed sources, respecting the two-request budget; ordinary rapid clicks start zero fixture preloads.
Actual ButtonPressLock remains enabled for POST/mutation forms in behavioral tests.
Preload tests cover authorization, actor/scope isolation, exact date/cache-key sharing, full pagination, and failure recovery.
verification.limitation: Fault injection and access-change isolation use automated mocks/isolated browser fixtures. Live portal checks used owner access and did not modify production permissions or business data.

remaining_delay_and_tradeoffs: Warm reports: fresh authorization about 112–190ms in final filter/tab samples; data loading about 2–3ms. Authentication was deliberately left uncached.
Cold report: around 2 seconds in final sample, with 1.28 seconds data loading and 0.59 seconds authentication. Network variance is material.

Dashboard: payroll-status query chain was 720ms of a 1.64-second click; Orders: data reads about 696ms of a 935ms click. Potential later work should profile these chains independently before changing their data semantics.

Preloading cannot guarantee an instant first visit and may overlap a cold query when a user clicks after a preload has already begun. It never blocks navigation; no speculative shared authorization-bearing page cache was introduced.

Existing raw report data freshness remains 30 seconds for external/out-of-band changes and immediate local invalidation for relevant application mutations; open reports remain snapshots until refreshed.

Next's existing back/forward Router Cache behavior remains. History restoration is not claimed to reauthenticate on every restore; new router pushes and preload requests perform their existing server permission checks.
development_note: Deleting route loading files initially left stale generated loader entries in the running Next dev server. Touching the existing admin layout triggered recompilation; a fresh browser route tree then confirmed the final retention results. No server restart or deployment.
